title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. M is a rank-4 matrix algebra over a base scheme S (identified with M_2(O_S) via φ). G = GL(M) is the unit group (≅ GL(2)_S) and PG = G/G_m. Following the previous page, ρ, σ are sections of G. The scalar ambiguity has been normalised so that Tr(ρ+σ)=1, and (40) presumably says that ρ+σ is an elementary projector P (rank 1, trace 1). The aim of this part of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' is to describe the scheme of pairs (ρ,σ) and their lifts from (ρ̃,σ̃) in PG. The ε_i are products such as ε_1 = −ρσ^{-1}, ε_0 = −σρ^{-1}, required to be regular unipotent. These are parabolic local monodromies, i.e. the P^1−{0,1,∞} / triangle-group (modular-group) situation underlying the loop equation.

(41) Normal form. After conjugating, P = diag(0,1), and one can take ρ = [[0,1],[v,w]] and σ = [[0,−1],[v',w']]. The condition ρ+σ = P gives v' = −v and w' = 1−w. Here det ρ = det σ = −v, so v must be invertible.

(42) The page gives ε_0 = [[1,1/v],[0,1]], which is regular unipotent because 1/v is a unit.

Open question. He asks (rewritten from a crossed-out sentence) whether ρ,σ are unique given ρ̃,σ̃, under the conditions ε_1 = −ρσ^{-1} and (40). He postpones this.

Digression (43). He first wants to check an assertion used several times before: G → PG induces a bijection on regular unipotent sections. Surjectivity holds by definition, as the margin note says: a section of PG is regular unipotent if fppf-locally it is induced by a regular unipotent section of G. Injectivity amounts to the following. If ε' = λε with λ ∈ Γ(G_m) and both are regular unipotent, then:
- determinants give λ² = 1, which is (44);
- traces give 2λ = 2, which is (45) on the next page.
Writing λ = 1+ν, this becomes 2ν = 0 and ν² = 0. So injectivity over S holds iff O_S has no nonzero section killed by 2 with square zero. This is true if 2 is invertible, and also if S is reduced. It fails, for example, over F_2[ν]/(ν²).

The obstruction group scheme H'_2 = Spec Z[T]/(T²−1, 2T−2) ≅ Spec Z[S]/(S², 2S) = Spec(Z ⊕ Z/2Z), the dual numbers on the module Z/2. It is the closed subgroup of μ_2 cutting out these λ. Fibres of the map on regular unipotents are torsors under H'_2.
errors: The formula for ε_0 does not match the stated convention. With ρ, σ as in (41), the convention written here, ε_0 = −σρ^{-1}, gives [[1,0],[−1,1]], a constant independent of v and w. Formula (42), [[1,1/v],[0,1]], is instead −σ^{-1}ρ, which agrees with the previous page's convention ε_1 = −σ^{-1}ρ. The two pages use inconsistent orderings. Both results are regular unipotent, so nothing downstream breaks.

Next page: Grothendieck inserts that H'_2 is 'plat sur Z'. But Z[S]/(S², 2S) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/2 as a Z-module, which has torsion, so H'_2 is finite but NOT flat over Z. Its fibre over Q is trivial (rank 1), while over F_2 it is μ_2 (rank 2).

Next page, minor imprecision: 'en car. 2 ou sur un schéma non réduit'. Failure of injectivity needs both 2-torsion in O_S and nilpotents; in characteristic 2 on a reduced scheme the map is still injective.
Implicit hypothesis on this page: det ρ = −v must be invertible for ε_0 to make sense; this is presumably guaranteed by ρ ∈ G.

ideas.what: Normal form for a pair (ρ,σ) in GL_2 whose sum is a rank-one idempotent, obtained by conjugation
ideas.modern_name: normal form / companion-type matrices for pairs; moduli of 2-dim representations of a free group up to conjugation
ideas.where_published: related themes in La Longue Marche (unpublished circulated typescript); not this computation

ideas.what: Regular unipotent sections of PGL_2, defined as fppf-locally lifted from GL_2, and the question of whether GL_2 → PGL_2 is injective on them
ideas.modern_name: regular unipotent elements over arbitrary base; lifting through central isogeny / G_m-quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA3 framework (Demazure–Grothendieck), Springer, Steinberg for regular unipotents
ideas.where_published: SGA3 treats reductive group schemes over general bases; this specific statement unsure

ideas.what: Obstruction scheme H'_2 = Spec Z[T]/(T²−1, 2T−2) ≅ Spec(Z ⊕ Z/2), the subgroup of μ_2 of scalars preserving unipotency
ideas.modern_name: non-flat finite subgroup scheme of μ_2 over Z; 'dual numbers' on Z/2

missed.claim: He raises, then postpones, whether ρ,σ are uniquely determined by their images in PG together with the conditions ε_1 = −ρσ^{-1} and (40). This is effectively an integral (over Z) uniqueness-of-lift question for parabolic GL_2-representations of the loop / triangle group. Its answer depends on the same 2-torsion nilpotent obstruction, but the page does not settle it.
missed.quote: Y a-t-il unicité de ρ, σ au donné de ρ̃, σ̃, par les conditions ε_1 = −ρσ^{-1} ... et (40)?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: lifting PGL_2 local systems with unipotent monodromy to GL_2 over Z, including at 2, is understood by specialists. The integral subtlety at 2 is a small detail.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine normal-form computation plus a standard check that scalar twisting preserves regular unipotency except over bases with 2-torsion nilpotents. It is correct apart from a convention slip and a mistaken 'flat' claim on the next page. Nothing here seems absent from the literature in a meaningful way.
transcription_corrections: The inserted question reads more likely 'Y a-t-il unicité de ρ, σ au donné de ρ̃, σ̃' (lifts of given images in PG), not 'au conjugué de ρ', σ''.
'(ou revêtements locales ...)' is more plausibly '(au moins localement ...)'.
Margin note: 'Donc, on dira qu'une section de PG est unipotente régulière si elle est loc. (fppf) induite d'une section de G unipotente régulière'.
'la surjectivité de cette application provient ici de la définition des unipotents réguliers de PG' (the transcription splits it awkwardly).
'savoir que l'homomorphisme' follows 'Je voudrais d'abord vérifier encore une assertion faite par en bas un certain nb de fois'.
